# @acme/tiny-cache

A tiny in-memory LRU cache for TypeScript. Zero dependencies, ~1KB gzipped, async-friendly.

Built because we were tired of pulling in 30KB of `lru-cache` for what amounts to a Map with a size cap. If you need stampede protection, TTL jitter, or persistence, use a real cache.

## Status

Used in production at Acme since 2024. Semver-stable. Node 18+ and modern evergreen browsers only — no IE, no Node 16.

## Quickstart

```ts
import { TinyCache } from '@acme/tiny-cache';

const cache = new TinyCache<string, number>({ max: 100 });

cache.set('a', 1);
cache.set('b', 2);

cache.get('a'); // 1
cache.has('b'); // true
cache.size;     // 2

cache.delete('a');
cache.clear();
```

Async loader pattern:

```ts
const users = new TinyCache<string, User>({ max: 500, ttlMs: 60_000 });

async function getUser(id: string): Promise<User> {
  const hit = users.get(id);
  if (hit) return hit;
  const fresh = await db.users.findById(id);
  users.set(id, fresh);
  return fresh;
}
```

TTL expiry happens lazily on `get`. If you want sweep-style eviction, drive a `setInterval` over `cache.keys()` yourself — we intentionally do not spawn timers.

## Features

- LRU eviction once `max` is reached.
- Optional per-entry `ttlMs`; expired entries are evicted lazily on access.
- Sync API — no `await` on `get` / `set` / `delete`.
- No dependencies. Works in Node 18+ and modern browsers.
- Ships ESM + CJS + `.d.ts`.
- `onEvict` callback fires with a reason (`size`, `ttl`, or `manual`).

## Options

| option        | type     | default | meaning                                |
|---------------|----------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `max`         | `number` | `1000`  | maximum number of entries              |
| `ttlMs`       | `number` | `0`     | default TTL per entry; `0` disables it |
| `onEvict`     | `fn`     | `noop`  | called with `(key, value, reason)`     |

All options are read at construction time. Mutating the options object after the fact has no effect.

## When not to use this

- You need persistence across process restarts → use Redis.
- You need cross-process sharing → use Redis or a shared store.
- You need cache-stampede protection (request coalescing) → wrap with `p-memoize` or roll your own.
- You need size-based eviction in bytes, not entries → not implemented, no plans to.
- You need weak-reference keys → use a `WeakMap`.

## Benchmarks

A back-of-the-envelope microbench on a Mac M2, Node 20, 1M random `get`/`set` on a cache of `max: 10_000`:

```
@acme/tiny-cache   ~14ns / op
lru-cache (v10)    ~22ns / op
Map (no eviction)  ~9ns / op
```

Take these numbers with a fistful of salt — your real workload will be dominated by what you do _around_ the cache, not the cache itself.

## FAQ

**Q: Why not just use a `Map`?** Because a `Map` grows forever. This adds an LRU policy and TTL on top and stops there.

**Q: Will you add async loaders / `getOrLoad`?** No. Compose it yourself in three lines (see Quickstart). Keeping the surface tiny is the point.
